posts.headlineEn: A new year. A new reader.
posts.headlineHt: Yon nouvo ane. Yon nouvo lektè.
posts.captionEn:
Haiti welcomed 2027 the way it always does, with soup joumou and the memory of independence. This year we have one wish for every child in rural Haiti: a book in her own language, and a library close enough to walk to.

Over 3,000 PILH Kreyòl books are already in children's hands. Help us put the next one there.
posts.captionHt:
Ayiti resevwa 2027 jan li toujou fè l, ak soup joumou ak souvni endepandans lan. Ane sa a nou gen yon sèl rèv pou chak timoun nan zòn riral: yon liv nan lang pa l, ak yon bibliyotèk ase pre pou l mache ale.

Plis pase 3,000 liv kreyòl PILH deja nan men timoun. Ede nou mete pwochen an.
posts.xEn: Haiti welcomed 2027 with soup joumou. Our wish for every child in rural Haiti: a book in her own language and a library she can walk to. 3,000+ Kreyòl books given so far.
posts.xHt: Ayiti resevwa 2027 ak soup joumou. Rèv nou pou chak timoun: yon liv nan lang pa l ak yon bibliyotèk li ka mache ale. Plis pase 3,000 liv kreyòl deja bay.

posts.captionEn:
Where does your support go? To five village libraries PILH mentors across the Ouest, the Centre and the Artibonite: Duplan, Cange, La Chapelle, Ravine Sèche and the Summits Education library system.

Two offer full services. All five put Kreyòl books within reach of children who had none. Meet them this month.
posts.captionHt:
Ki kote sipò ou ale? Nan senk bibliyotèk vilaj PILH akonpaye nan Lwès, Sant ak Latibonit: Duplan, Kanj, La Chapelle, Ravine Sèche ak rezo bibliyotèk Summits Education.

De ladan yo ofri tout sèvis. Tou senk mete liv kreyòl nan men timoun ki pa t genyen. Vin rankontre yo mwa sa a.
posts.xEn: Your support reaches 5 village libraries in Haiti's Ouest, Centre and Artibonite: Duplan, Cange, La Chapelle, Ravine Sèche and Summits Education. Meet them this month.
posts.xHt: Sipò ou rive nan 5 bibliyotèk vilaj nan Lwès, Sant ak Latibonit: Duplan, Kanj, La Chapelle, Ravine Sèche ak Summits Education.

posts.captionEn:
One resolution that keeps itself: join Klib Liv la, the PILH Book Club. Members give from $15 a month, which buys ten Kreyòl children's books every single month.

Zeffy passes 100% of your gift to PILH, and your tax receipt arrives the same minute.
posts.captionHt:
Yon rezolisyon ki kenbe tèt li: antre nan Klib Liv la. Manm yo bay apati $15 pa mwa, sa achte dis liv kreyòl pou timoun chak mwa.

Zeffy pase 100% don ou bay PILH, epi resi taks ou rive menm minit lan.
posts.xEn: A resolution that keeps itself: join Klib Liv la. $15 a month buys 10 Kreyòl children's books, every month. 100% reaches PILH.
posts.xHt: Yon rezolisyon ki kenbe tèt li: Klib Liv la. $15 pa mwa achte 10 liv kreyòl chak mwa. 100% rive nan PILH.

posts.captionEn:
Tomorrow marks seventeen years since the January 12 earthquake. We hold every family who lost someone in our hearts.

Schools fell that day, and so did the books inside them. Rebuilding has always meant more than walls. It means a child back at a table with a story in her hands.
posts.captionHt:
Demen fè disèt ane depi tranblemanntè 12 janvye a. Nou kenbe chak fanmi ki te pèdi moun nan kè nou.

Lekòl te tonbe jou sa a, ak liv ki te ladan yo. Rebati pa janm sèlman miray. Se yon timoun ki retounen sou yon tab ak yon istwa nan men l.
posts.xEn: Tomorrow marks 17 years since the January 12 earthquake. We hold every family who lost someone in our hearts.
posts.xHt: Demen fè 17 ane depi tranblemanntè 12 janvye a. Nou kenbe chak fanmi nan kè nou.
posts.needs: Tone check: remembrance only, no donation ask on this post.

posts.captionEn:
Our flagship project. Pastor Edzaire Paul founded the Duplan library more than twenty years ago. In 2022, at the village's request, PILH began rebuilding it as a modern children's library and a future training center for library workers across Haiti.

A signed agreement with the village governance committee frames every step.
posts.captionHt:
Pwojè vedèt nou. Pastè Edzaire Paul te fonde bibliyotèk Duplan plis pase ven ane de sa. An 2022, sou demann vilaj la, PILH kòmanse rebati l kòm yon bibliyotèk modèn pou timoun ak yon fiti sant fòmasyon pou travayè bibliyotèk nan tout peyi a.

Yon akò siyen ak komite vilaj la gide chak etap.
posts.xEn: Our flagship: Duplan's 20 year old village library, rebuilt since 2022 as a modern children's library and future training center for Haiti's library workers.
posts.xHt: Pwojè vedèt nou: bibliyotèk Duplan, ki gen plis pase 20 ane, n ap rebati l depi 2022 pou timoun ak fòmasyon travayè bibliyotèk.
posts.needs: Swap in a sharper Duplan photo (current file is 320 px wide).

posts.captionEn:
Computers and a reliable power source turn a room of books into a library that can train the next generation of Haitian library workers.

$1,000 equips Duplan with both. Gifts of any size move it forward.
posts.captionHt:
Òdinatè ak yon sous kouran solid fè yon chanm liv tounen yon bibliyotèk ki ka fòme pwochen jenerasyon travayè bibliyotèk ayisyen.

$1,000 bay Duplan toude. Nenpòt don fè l avanse.
posts.xEn: $1,000 gives the Duplan library computers and a power source, so it can train Haiti's next library workers. Every gift moves it forward.
posts.xHt: $1,000 bay bibliyotèk Duplan òdinatè ak kouran pou l fòme travayè bibliyotèk. Chak don konte.

posts.headlineHt: Li ak yon timoun jodi a
posts.captionEn:
On this day of service, the simplest service of all: read with a child.

At our early literacy book celebration, children under six went home with free books in Kreyòl, French, Spanish and English. For many it was the first book they ever owned. Tell us who you are reading with today.
posts.captionHt:
Jou sèvis sa a, pi senp sèvis la: li ak yon timoun.

Nan fèt liv nou pou timoun piti, timoun ki poko gen sizan te ale lakay ak liv gratis an kreyòl, franse, panyòl ak angle. Pou anpil ladan yo, se te premye liv yo. Di nou ak ki moun w ap li jodi a.
posts.xEn: On this day of service, the simplest service of all: read with a child. Who are you reading with today?
posts.xHt: Jou sèvis sa a: li ak yon timoun. Ak ki moun w ap li jodi a?

posts.headlineHt: Ravine Sèche: timoun yo kouri vini
posts.captionEn:
Ravine Sèche is a tiny village of 150 houses in the Artibonite. In 2020 PILH funded new books and arranged three days of training for Edson Fanfan, the reading center's dedicated library worker.

Today, the village supervisor says, kids stream in as soon as the doors open. They read stories, then retell them to one another.
posts.captionHt:
Ravine Sèche se yon ti vilaj 150 kay nan Latibonit. An 2020 PILH finanse nouvo liv epi òganize twa jou fòmasyon pou Edson Fanfan, travayè bibliyotèk sant lekti a.

Jodi a, sipèvizè vilaj la di timoun yo kouri antre depi pòt la louvri. Yo li istwa, epi yo rakonte yo youn bay lòt.
posts.xEn: In Ravine Sèche, a village of 150 houses, kids now stream into the reading center the moment it opens, then retell the stories to each other.
posts.xHt: Nan Ravine Sèche, timoun yo kouri antre nan sant lekti a depi l louvri, epi yo rakonte istwa yo youn bay lòt.

posts.captionEn:
Before you give, check us. PILH holds Candid's Platinum Seal of Transparency, and every annual report since 2022 is one click away on our site.

An all volunteer board, books bought in Haiti whenever we can, and 100% of Zeffy gifts reaching our programs.
posts.captionHt:
Anvan ou bay, verifye nou. PILH gen Sele Platinum Candid pou transparans, epi tout rapò anyèl depi 2022 a yon klik sou sit nou.

Yon konsèy volontè, liv nou achte ann Ayiti chak fwa nou kapab, ak 100% don Zeffy ki rive nan pwogram yo.
posts.xEn: Before you give, check us. Candid Platinum Seal, every annual report public, an all volunteer board.
posts.xHt: Anvan ou bay, verifye nou. Sele Platinum Candid, tout rapò anyèl piblik, yon konsèy volontè.

posts.captionEn:
A young reader wrote to us after receiving her PILH books. Her favorite was Istwa Konpè Kra ak Konpè Po. The lesson she took: never give up, and fight for your dreams.

Her dream is to write a book one day. Ours is to make sure she has a library to write it in.
posts.captionHt:
Yon jèn lektè ekri nou apre li fin resevwa liv PILH li yo. Sa li pi renmen an se Istwa Konpè Kra ak Konpè Po. Leson li aprann: pa janm bay legen, goumen pou rèv ou.

Rèv li se ekri yon liv yon jou. Rèv pa nou se pou l gen yon bibliyotèk pou l ekri l.
posts.xEn: A young reader's favorite PILH book taught her: never give up. Her dream is to write a book. Ours is to give her a library to write it in.
posts.xHt: Liv PILH yon jèn lektè te pi renmen an aprann li: pa janm bay legen. Rèv li se ekri yon liv.

posts.captionEn:
The Alfabè Kreyòl Mwen alphabet chart took thirteen years to perfect, working with MIT linguists. It has reached 98 schools, 95 teachers and 3,800 students.

When we found rural classrooms with no charts at all, we made our own.
posts.captionHt:
Tablo alfabè Alfabè Kreyòl Mwen pran trèz ane pou l fin bon, ak lengwis MIT. Li rive nan 98 lekòl, 95 pwofesè ak 3,800 elèv.

Lè nou jwenn sal klas riral san okenn tablo, nou fè pa nou.
posts.xEn: Our Alfabè Kreyòl Mwen chart took 13 years with MIT linguists. It's now in 98 schools, reaching 95 teachers and 3,800 students.
posts.xHt: Tablo Alfabè Kreyòl Mwen an pran 13 ane ak lengwis MIT. Li nan 98 lekòl, 3,800 elèv.

posts.captionEn:
One wall chart changes a classroom for years. $100 puts four Kreyòl alphabet charts in four classrooms that have none.

Close January with a gift every student will see every morning.
posts.captionHt:
Yon tablo sou miray chanje yon sal klas pou plizyè ane. $100 mete kat tablo alfabè kreyòl nan kat sal klas ki pa genyen.

Fèmen janvye ak yon don chak elèv ap wè chak maten.
posts.xEn: $100 puts four Kreyòl alphabet charts on four classroom walls that have none. A gift students see every morning.
posts.xHt: $100 mete kat tablo alfabè kreyòl nan kat sal klas. Yon don elèv yo wè chak maten.

posts.headlineHt: 95% pale kreyòl. Liv yo pa pale l.
posts.captionEn:
This month is about one idea: children learn to read best in the language they speak at home.

Ninety five percent of Haitians speak Kreyòl. At most one in ten speaks French. Yet almost every book in Haiti's schools is in French. That gap is where PILH works.
posts.captionHt:
Mwa sa a se pou yon sèl lide: timoun aprann li pi byen nan lang yo pale lakay yo.

Katrevenkenz pousan ayisyen pale kreyòl. Pa plis pase youn sou dis pale franse. Men prèske tout liv nan lekòl yo an franse. Se nan twou sa a PILH travay.
posts.xEn: 95% of Haitians speak Kreyòl. At most 1 in 10 speaks French. Almost every school book is in French. That gap is where we work.
posts.xHt: 95% ayisyen pale kreyòl. Prèske tout liv lekòl an franse. Se la PILH travay.

posts.captionEn:
It's World Read Aloud Day. The best thing a parent can do for a future reader costs nothing: read aloud, every day, in the language of home.

A child's brain builds itself most intensively from birth to age four. In Haiti, that window opens in Kreyòl.
posts.captionHt:
Se Jounen Mondyal Lekti a Vwa Wo. Pi bon bagay yon paran ka fè pou yon fiti lektè pa koute anyen: li fò chak jou, nan lang lakay la.

Sèvo yon timoun bati tèt li pi plis depi li fèt rive kat an. Ann Ayiti, fenèt sa a louvri an kreyòl.
posts.xEn: It's World Read Aloud Day. Read aloud today, in the language of home. In Haiti that language is Kreyòl.
posts.xHt: Se Jounen Lekti a Vwa Wo. Li fò jodi a, nan lang lakay. Ann Ayiti se kreyòl.
posts.needs: Confirm World Read Aloud Day date for 2027 (usually the first Wednesday of February).

posts.captionEn:
A child who reads her first story in Kreyòl reads the next one faster. $25 buys a set of three Haitian Kreyòl storybooks for a village library.

Give in English, French, Spanish or Kreyòl. Our form speaks all four.
posts.captionHt:
Yon timoun ki li premye istwa l an kreyòl li pwochen an pi vit. $25 achte yon seri twa liv istwa kreyòl pou yon bibliyotèk vilaj.

Bay an angle, franse, panyòl oswa kreyòl. Fòm nou an pale tou kat.
posts.xEn: $25 buys three Haitian Kreyòl storybooks for a village library. A child who reads her first story in Kreyòl reads the next one faster.
posts.xHt: $25 achte twa liv istwa kreyòl pou yon bibliyotèk vilaj.

posts.headlineEn: Meet Jesula. She learns to read.
posts.headlineHt: Men Jesula. L ap aprann li.
posts.captionEn:
Jesula Ap Apran Li is one of the six easy readers PILH co published with Haitian illustrators and translators. Carline visits Jesula's village every year with new books. Jesula learns to read, shares the gift with her village, and grows into a successful young woman.

Every page was edited by Haitian linguists.
posts.captionHt:
Jesula Ap Apran Li se youn nan sis ti liv fasil PILH pibliye ak desinatè ak tradiktè ayisyen. Carline vizite vilaj Jesula chak ane ak nouvo liv. Jesula aprann li, li pataje kado a ak vilaj li, epi li grandi tounen yon jèn fanm ki reyisi.

Lengwis ayisyen korije chak paj.
posts.xEn: Meet Jesula, star of one of our six Kreyòl easy readers. She learns to read, shares it with her village, and grows into a successful young woman.
posts.xHt: Men Jesula, nan youn nan sis liv kreyòl nou yo. Li aprann li epi li pataje l ak vilaj li.

posts.captionEn:
For generations, Haitian children were taught to read in colonial French, by rote, in a language most of them never spoke at home. Struggling readers gave up.

PILH's approach: Kreyòl first, and French as the bridge in school. Joy comes first, and it comes in Kreyòl.
posts.captionHt:
Pandan plizyè jenerasyon, timoun ayisyen te aprann li an franse kolonyal, pa kè, nan yon lang pifò pa t pale lakay yo. Lektè ki t ap lite yo te bay legen.

Apwòch PILH: kreyòl an premye, franse kòm pon nan lekòl. Plezi a vini anvan, epi li vini an kreyòl.
posts.xEn: Generations of Haitian children learned to read by rote in French, a language most never spoke at home. Our approach: Kreyòl first, French as the bridge.
posts.xHt: Plizyè jenerasyon aprann li pa kè an franse. Apwòch nou: kreyòl an premye, franse kòm pon.

posts.headlineEn: Give a book you'll never read
posts.headlineHt: Bay yon liv ou p ap janm li
posts.captionEn:
This Valentine's weekend, give a love letter in Kreyòl. A gift in honor of someone you love puts a book in a child's hands in their name, and we send them a note.

Ten books start at $15.
posts.captionHt:
Wikenn Sen Valanten sa a, bay yon lèt damou an kreyòl. Yon don nan non yon moun ou renmen mete yon liv nan men yon timoun, epi nou voye yon ti mo ba yo.

Dis liv kòmanse a $15.
posts.xEn: This Valentine's weekend, give in honor of someone you love. A Kreyòl book goes to a child in their name.
posts.xHt: Wikenn Sen Valanten an, bay nan non yon moun ou renmen. Yon liv kreyòl rive nan men yon timoun.

posts.headlineEn: Soup joumou and a story of freedom
posts.captionEn:
In Malachi Bay Tout Vilaj La Manje, Malachi plants seeds he finds by the river. They grow into the squash for soup joumou, and the whole village gathers to share the soup and the story of Haitian independence.

History sticks when a child reads it in her own language.
posts.captionHt:
Nan Malachi Bay Tout Vilaj La Manje, Malachi plante grenn li jwenn bò larivyè. Yo bay joumou pou soup joumou, epi tout vilaj la reyini pou pataje soup la ak istwa endepandans Ayiti.

Istwa rete nan tèt lè yon timoun li l nan lang pa l.
posts.xEn: In one of our Kreyòl readers, Malachi's seeds become soup joumou and the village shares the story of Haitian independence.
posts.xHt: Nan liv Malachi a, grenn yo tounen soup joumou epi vilaj la pataje istwa endepandans lan.

posts.captionEn:
We walked through 32 classrooms in six rural schools and found not one storybook, not one bookshelf.

We call them book deserts. Seventy percent of Haiti's primary schools are private and rarely budget for reading for pleasure. A library or book corner nearby changes everything.
posts.captionHt:
Nou mache nan 32 sal klas nan sis lekòl riral epi nou pa jwenn yon sèl liv istwa, yon sèl etajè.

Nou rele yo dezè liv. Swasanndis pousan lekòl primè ann Ayiti prive, epi yo raman gen bidjè pou lekti plezi. Yon bibliyotèk oswa yon kwen liv toupre chanje tout bagay.
posts.xEn: We walked through 32 rural classrooms in Haiti and found zero storybooks. We call them book deserts.
posts.xHt: Nou vizite 32 sal klas riral epi nou jwenn zewo liv istwa. Nou rele yo dezè liv.

posts.captionEn:
This Sunday, February 21, the world celebrates International Mother Language Day. For Haiti's children, that language is Kreyòl.

Celebrate it with a gift that lasts all year: Klib Liv la membership from $15 a month, ten Kreyòl books every month.
posts.captionHt:
Dimanch sa a, 21 fevriye, mond lan selebre Jounen Entènasyonal Lang Manman. Pou timoun Ayiti, lang sa a se kreyòl.

Selebre l ak yon don ki dire tout ane a: Klib Liv la apati $15 pa mwa, dis liv kreyòl chak mwa.
posts.xEn: Sunday is International Mother Language Day. For Haiti's children that language is Kreyòl. Celebrate with Klib Liv la, 10 books a month from $15.
posts.xHt: Dimanch se Jounen Lang Manman. Pou timoun Ayiti, se kreyòl. Selebre ak Klib Liv la.

posts.captionEn:
Serafina the donkey would rather play with children than work, until her friend Joseph finds the job that is perfect for her.

It's one of our six Kreyòl easy readers, and one of the most borrowed. Funny, familiar and in the language children dream in.
posts.captionHt:
Bourik Serafina pito jwe ak timoun pase travay, jiskaske zanmi l Joseph jwenn travay ki fèt pou li.

Se youn nan sis ti liv kreyòl nou yo, epi youn timoun yo prete plis. Komik, abitye, epi nan lang timoun yo reve.
posts.xEn: Serafina the donkey would rather play than work, until Joseph finds the perfect job for her. One of our most loved Kreyòl readers.
posts.xHt: Bourik Serafina pito jwe pase travay. Youn nan liv kreyòl timoun yo pi renmen.

posts.captionEn:
The Haiti Libraries Alliance connects library workers inside Haiti and around the world. PILH started it in 2020 with the Mortenson Center at the University of Illinois.

Monthly Zoom meetings since 2021, 12 member libraries and growing, and membership is free.
posts.captionHt:
Alyans Bibliyotèk Ayiti konekte travayè bibliyotèk ann Ayiti ak toupatou nan mond lan. PILH lanse l an 2020 ak Mortenson Center nan University of Illinois.

Reyinyon Zoom chak mwa depi 2021, 12 bibliyotèk manm k ap grandi, epi manm gratis.
posts.xEn: The Haiti Libraries Alliance: 12 member libraries, monthly Zoom meetings since 2021, free to join. A PILH and University of Illinois collaboration.
posts.xHt: Alyans Bibliyotèk Ayiti: 12 bibliyotèk manm, reyinyon chak mwa, gratis.

posts.headlineEn: Library worker in Haiti? Join us.
posts.captionEn:
Do you run a library, a reading corner or a school collection in Haiti? The Haiti Libraries Alliance is free, meets monthly on Zoom, and shares guides and training in Kreyòl, French and English.

Share this with a librarian you know.
posts.captionHt:
Èske w ap jere yon bibliyotèk, yon kwen lekti oswa liv yon lekòl ann Ayiti? Alyans Bibliyotèk Ayiti gratis, li reyini chak mwa sou Zoom, epi li pataje gid ak fòmasyon an kreyòl, franse ak angle.

Pataje sa ak yon bibliyotekè ou konnen.
posts.xEn: Run a library or reading corner in Haiti? The Haiti Libraries Alliance is free and meets monthly. Share with a librarian you know.
posts.xHt: Ou jere yon bibliyotèk ann Ayiti? Alyans lan gratis epi li reyini chak mwa. Pataje l.

posts.headlineEn: She taught herself to be a librarian
posts.headlineHt: Li aprann bibliyotèk pou kont li
posts.captionEn:
Meet Beverly Stephen, lead library worker at Duplan. She taught herself library skills from the internet before she ever had formal training. Her goal: become a librarian.

This month we celebrate the women who build readers in rural Haiti.
posts.captionHt:
Men Beverly Stephen, travayè bibliyotèk prensipal Duplan. Li aprann travay bibliyotèk sou entènèt anvan li te janm gen fòmasyon. Objektif li: vin bibliyotekè.

Mwa sa a nou selebre fanm k ap bati lektè nan zòn riral Ayiti.
posts.xEn: Meet Beverly Stephen. She taught herself library skills online before any formal training. Her goal: become a librarian. This month, we celebrate the women who build readers.
posts.xHt: Men Beverly Stephen. Li aprann travay bibliyotèk sou entènèt. Objektif li: vin bibliyotekè.

posts.headlineEn: A doctor who chairs a library
posts.headlineHt: Yon doktè ki dirije yon bibliyotèk
posts.captionEn:
Dr. Beatrice Gaunthier is a clinical internist. She also chairs the Duplan library committee and reports its progress to PILH.

Community ownership is how a library lasts. Duplan is run by its village, for its village.
posts.captionHt:
Doktè Beatrice Gaunthier se yon doktè medsin entèn. Li prezide komite bibliyotèk Duplan tou epi li rapòte pwogrè l bay PILH.

Se lè kominote a mèt bibliyotèk la li dire. Se vilaj la k ap mennen Duplan, pou vilaj la.
posts.xEn: Dr. Beatrice Gaunthier is a clinical internist who also chairs the Duplan library committee. Community ownership is how a library lasts.
posts.xHt: Doktè Beatrice Gaunthier, doktè, prezide komite bibliyotèk Duplan. Kominote a mèt bibliyotèk la.
posts.needs: Swap in a sharper Duplan photo (current file is 320 px wide).

posts.captionEn:
Librarians are the heart of a library. $250 funds a month of a librarian's stipend and literacy workshops.

This Women's History Month, invest in the women who keep the doors open.
posts.captionHt:
Bibliyotekè yo se kè yon bibliyotèk. $250 peye yon mwa bous yon bibliyotekè ak atelye alfabetizasyon.

Mwa istwa fanm sa a, envesti nan fanm ki kenbe pòt yo louvri.
posts.xEn: $250 funds a month of a librarian's stipend and literacy workshops. Invest in the women who keep Haiti's village libraries open.
posts.xHt: $250 peye yon mwa bous yon bibliyotekè. Envesti nan fanm ki kenbe bibliyotèk yo louvri.

posts.headlineEn: A girl who reads changes a village
posts.headlineHt: Yon tifi ki li chanje yon vilaj
posts.captionEn:
Happy International Women's Day. Every woman in our story started as a girl with a book: the library workers, the committee chairs, the translators, the teachers.

Nearly four in ten Haitian adults cannot read. The surest way to change that starts with the girls reading today.
posts.captionHt:
Bòn fèt Jounen Entènasyonal Fanm. Chak fanm nan istwa nou te kòmanse kòm yon tifi ak yon liv: travayè bibliyotèk yo, prezidan komite yo, tradiktè yo, pwofesè yo.

Prèske kat sou dis granmoun ayisyen pa konn li. Pi bon fason pou chanje sa kòmanse ak tifi k ap li jodi a.
posts.xEn: Happy International Women's Day. Every woman in our story started as a girl with a book. Change starts with the girls reading today.
posts.xHt: Bòn fèt Jounen Fanm. Chak fanm nan istwa nou te kòmanse kòm yon tifi ak yon liv.

posts.headlineEn: She translated our books into Kreyòl
posts.headlineHt: Li tradui liv nou yo an kreyòl
posts.captionEn:
Michaëlle Saint-Natus mentors the Ravine Sèche Reading Center. In 2019 she volunteered to translate PILH's book collection into Kreyòl, and she shares her expertise with every library that asks.

Cooperation like hers is what rural Haiti's libraries need everywhere.
posts.captionHt:
Michaëlle Saint-Natus se mantò Sant Lekti Ravine Sèche. An 2019 li te pòte l volontè pou tradui koleksyon liv PILH an kreyòl, epi li pataje konesans li ak chak bibliyotèk ki mande.

Koperasyon tankou pa l la se sa bibliyotèk riral Ayiti bezwen toupatou.
posts.xEn: Michaëlle Saint-Natus volunteered to translate our book collection into Kreyòl and mentors the Ravine Sèche Reading Center.
posts.xHt: Michaëlle Saint-Natus tradui liv nou yo an kreyòl epi li se mantò Sant Lekti Ravine Sèche.

posts.captionEn:
A trained library worker serves a village for years. $400 provides a full set of training materials for one library worker.

Edson Fanfan trained for three days and came home ready to catalogue the collection and run reading contests. Train the next one.
posts.captionHt:
Yon travayè bibliyotèk ki fòme sèvi yon vilaj pandan plizyè ane. $400 bay yon seri materyèl fòmasyon konplè pou yon travayè bibliyotèk.

Edson Fanfan fè twa jou fòmasyon epi li tounen pare pou klase koleksyon an ak òganize konkou lekti. Fòme pwochen an.
posts.xEn: $400 gives one Haitian library worker a full set of training materials. A trained library worker serves a village for years.
posts.xHt: $400 bay yon travayè bibliyotèk materyèl fòmasyon konplè.

posts.captionEn:
Judeline Marechal joined the Duplan library as assistant librarian in spring 2023 with one stated goal: improve young children's education.

She and Beverly are building what Duplan will become, a children's library and a training center for the whole country.
posts.captionHt:
Judeline Marechal antre nan bibliyotèk Duplan kòm asistan bibliyotekè nan prentan 2023 ak yon sèl objektif: amelyore edikasyon timoun piti.

Avèk Beverly, l ap bati sa Duplan pral tounen, yon bibliyotèk pou timoun ak yon sant fòmasyon pou tout peyi a.
posts.xEn: Judeline Marechal joined Duplan in 2023 with one goal: improve young children's education. She and Beverly are building Haiti's next training library.
posts.xHt: Judeline Marechal antre Duplan an 2023 ak yon objektif: edikasyon timoun piti.

posts.captionEn:
At a Rotary leaders meeting in Haiti, Dr. Sara Currie Mansbach visited villages where children had never seen a picture book. She found a new life purpose.

That was the start of PILH. “Where there is no book, there is no reader. We start with the book.”
posts.captionHt:
Nan yon reyinyon lidè Rotary ann Ayiti, Doktè Sara Currie Mansbach vizite vilaj kote timoun pa t janm wè yon liv imaj. Li jwenn yon nouvo rezon pou l viv.

Se konsa PILH te kòmanse. “Kote ki pa gen liv, pa gen lektè. Nou kòmanse ak liv la.”
posts.xEn: PILH began when our founder, Dr. Sara Currie Mansbach, met children in Cange who had never seen a picture book. “We start with the book.”
posts.xHt: PILH kòmanse lè fondatè nou te rankontre timoun Kanj ki pa t janm wè yon liv imaj.

posts.headlineEn: Your skills can build a library
posts.headlineHt: Talan ou ka bati yon bibliyotèk
posts.captionEn:
PILH runs on volunteers: an eleven member all volunteer board and committees that meet on Zoom. We need help with grant writing, marketing and social media, events, volunteer recruiting and program design.

Give an hour a month. Tell us what you are good at.
posts.captionHt:
PILH mache ak volontè: yon konsèy onz manm ki tout volontè ak komite ki reyini sou Zoom. Nou bezwen èd pou ekri pwopozisyon, maketing ak rezo sosyal, evènman, rekrite volontè ak konsepsyon pwogram.

Bay yon èdtan pa mwa. Di nou sa ou konn fè.
posts.xEn: PILH runs on volunteers. We need help with grants, marketing, social media, events and program design. Give an hour a month.
posts.xHt: PILH mache ak volontè. Bay yon èdtan pa mwa. Di nou sa ou konn fè.

posts.captionEn:
The reader is built before the fifth birthday. PILH serves children from birth to eight, their families and their teachers.

That is why our libraries equip parents and caregivers, not just classrooms. Story time at home is where it starts.
posts.captionHt:
Lektè a bati anvan senkyèm anivèsè a. PILH sèvi timoun depi yo fèt rive uit an, fanmi yo ak pwofesè yo.

Se pou sa bibliyotèk nou yo ekipe paran ak moun k ap okipe timoun, pa sèlman sal klas. Se lè istwa lakay la tout bagay kòmanse.
posts.xEn: The reader is built before the fifth birthday. That's why our libraries equip parents and caregivers, not just classrooms.
posts.xHt: Lektè a bati anvan senkyèm anivèsè a. Bibliyotèk nou yo ekipe paran tou.

posts.captionEn:
What makes a library full service? Trained staff, a catalogued Kreyòl collection, programs for young children and families, and doors that open on a schedule the village can count on.

Duplan and Cange offer full services today. Our goal is to bring the others there.
posts.captionHt:
Kisa ki fè yon bibliyotèk ofri tout sèvis? Moun ki fòme, yon koleksyon liv kreyòl ki klase, pwogram pou timoun piti ak fanmi, ak pòt ki louvri lè vilaj la ka konte sou yo.

Duplan ak Kanj ofri tout sèvis jodi a. Objektif nou se mennen lòt yo la.
posts.xEn: Two of the five village libraries we mentor offer full services today: Duplan and Cange. Our goal is to bring the others there.
posts.xHt: Duplan ak Kanj ofri tout sèvis jodi a. Objektif nou se mennen lòt yo la.

posts.captionEn:
Many employers match charitable gifts, so your $50 becomes $100 for Haiti's village libraries. Ask your HR team and use our EIN: 87-0904773.

It takes five minutes and doubles your impact.
posts.captionHt:
Anpil patwon double don charitab, kidonk $50 ou tounen $100 pou bibliyotèk vilaj Ayiti. Mande ekip resous imen ou epi itilize EIN nou: 87-0904773.

Sa pran senk minit epi li double enpak ou.
posts.xEn: Many employers match gifts, so your $50 becomes $100 for Haiti's village libraries. Ask HR and use EIN 87-0904773.
posts.xHt: Anpil patwon double don. Mande resous imen epi itilize EIN 87-0904773.

posts.captionEn:
Thank you for reading with us this quarter: the libraries, the books, the women who keep the doors open, and the children who stream in.

Next month we take you inside the libraries during the season Haiti celebrates its flag and its heritage. Stay with us.
posts.captionHt:
Mèsi paske nou li ansanm trimès sa a: bibliyotèk yo, liv yo, fanm ki kenbe pòt yo louvri, ak timoun ki kouri antre.

Mwa pwochen n ap mennen nou anndan bibliyotèk yo pandan sezon Ayiti selebre drapo l ak eritaj li. Rete avè nou.
posts.xEn: Thank you for reading with us this quarter. Next: inside the libraries as Haiti celebrates its flag and heritage. Stay with us.
posts.xHt: Mèsi paske nou li ansanm trimès sa a. Rete avè nou.

posts.headlineEn: Be a founding Klib Liv la member
posts.headlineHt: Vin yon manm fondatè Klib Liv la
posts.captionEn:
Monthly givers are the heartbeat of this work, so we gave them a name: Klib Liv la. Members fund the books, the shelves and the librarians month after month, and get the library stories first in our newsletter.

Close the quarter as a member. $15 a month, ten Kreyòl books, every month.
posts.captionHt:
Moun ki bay chak mwa se batman kè travay sa a, se pou sa nou ba yo yon non: Klib Liv la. Manm yo finanse liv, etajè ak bibliyotekè mwa apre mwa, epi yo resevwa istwa bibliyotèk yo an premye nan bilten nou.

Fèmen trimès la kòm manm. $15 pa mwa, dis liv kreyòl, chak mwa.
posts.xEn: Monthly givers are the heartbeat of this work. Join Klib Liv la: $15 a month, 10 Kreyòl books, every month.
posts.xHt: Moun ki bay chak mwa se batman kè travay sa a. Antre nan Klib Liv la: $15 pa mwa.
